text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High 5xx spike detected for service=prod-gateway in us-east-1. 5xx_rate=7.9% (threshold 1.0%). Alert: infra.alerts.gateway. Identifiers: trace-sample low, missing request-id in ~35% of sampled requests.

miguel.l: ack — taking this. tagging @sre-oncall.

sre-oncall: on call. quick check: k8s node metrics look okay, CPU/GPU normal. Errors originate from gateway pod group gateway-prod-v3. Not seeing obvious OOMs.

miguel.l: reproducing: curl against /v1/health returns 200, but production traffic to /v1/complete shows 502/504s in access logs.

ops-bot: deploy-check: last deploy for gateway-prod v3 at 2100451200 by ci-pipeline. No rollbacks.

alice.chen: are the 5xx correlated with specific models or backend targets? any downstream timeouts?

miguel.l: preliminary traces (very sparse) show many requests timing out waiting on model-proxy upstream with upstream status=504. But we only have traces for ~5% of requests — sampling looks wrong.

eng-lead: note: customer-facing SLO window is 1m and currently showing 99.2% success over last 10m. We're within tolerance for now but trending bad. Need fast mitigations + better signal.

miguel.l: two immediate pain points: (1) trace/log sampling is low due to a config rollback we missed last month, (2) some gateway workers aren't emitting request_id header when backend closes early, so we lose correlatability.

support-ops: support queue already reports 12 errant sessions flagged by customers, +2 enterprise customers filing tickets. We should prepare a short customer-facing note if this persists >30m.

miguel.l: quick mitigation plan — short-term (hotpatch): increase trace sampling to 100% for gateway-prod for 20 minutes, force request_id injection in ingress filter, and enable extra gateway debug logging for backend response codes. Doing them in sequence to avoid log explosion.

sre-oncall: +1. steps?

miguel.l: running commands now:

```
# increase trace sampling to 100% for gateway-prod
kubectl -n prod patch configmap gateway-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"trace_sampling":"1.0"}}'

# patch envoy filter to always add x-request-id when missing
kubectl -n prod patch envoyfilter gateway-requestid --type merge -p '{"spec":{"filters":{"request_id":{"force":true}}}}'

# scale debug sidecars to 2 to avoid blocking
kubectl -n prod scale deployment/gateway-debug --replicas=2
```

ops-bot: configmap patched (2100456820). envoyfilter patched (2100456840). debug sidecar scaled (2100456855).

michael.l: (note: I pushed a small log-level bump, watchers please monitor log volume)

alice.chen: seeing trace sampling up in datadog -> new traces arriving. Correlation improved, I can now see request_id for previously opaque spans.

sre-oncall: initial pattern: about 60% of failing requests show upstream latency hitting 15s then connection reset. Looks like model-proxy node group mpool-east-2 having intermittent stalls.

miguel.l: temporary routing change: divert 30% of prod-gateway traffic to us-west region pool to reduce load on mpool-east-2. Applying traffic split via rollout policy.

```
# apply traffic split
redwoodctl route update gateway-prod --split '{"us-east-1":70, "us-west-2":30}' --reason "mitigate mpool-east-2 latency"
```

ops-bot: route update accepted (2100456880).

support-ops: performed a quick customer impact triage: ~2% of active users affected, majority seen in east coast customers. Drafting short advisory to impacted customers.

eng-lead: good. are we tracking the root cause? temp routing reduces 5xx to ~1.5% but still above baseline.

alice.chen: with traces at 100% we see mpool-east-2 process threads stuck on lock in model loader when certain request sizes arrive. Suspect recent model-rollout or config on mpool.

miguel.l: can we scale mpool-east-2 or restart a subset without customer-facing risk?

sre-oncall: safe approach: cordon one node then drain, restart mpool pods on drained node with restart policy. Doing a rolling restart of 1 node at a time.

```
kubectl -n models cordon node/mpool-east-2-03
kubectl -n models drain node/mpool-east-2-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
kubectl -n models rollout restart deployment/mpool-east-2
```

ops-bot: cordon/drain started (2100456905).

miguel.l: restarting shard 03 now. monitoring.

sre-oncall: after restart, observed reduction in 5xx to ~0.9% in 5m window. Good signal.

support-ops: customer advisory drafted and queued, will send if rate remains >1.0% at +15m.

miguel.l: follow-up actions (post-incident):
- restore trace_sampling to previous value (we set 1.0 temporarily)
- write a short patch to ensure request_id always created at ingress (permanent)
- add a regression test for model loader lock on specific request sizes
- investigate why sampling config rolled back earlier (CI gating?)

alice.chen: agreed. I'll take the permanent request_id patch + unit tests.

eng-lead: I will own the postmortem and customer comms with support-ops. Miguel, please include timeline and commands run.

miguel.l: handing off to @alice.chen for next on-call window (ends in 30m). Current runbook state: mitigations applied, traffic split in place, one mpool node restarted. 5xx back to ~0.9%.

alice.chen: taking handoff. I'll keep trace sampling at 100% for another 5m then step down to 20% while we confirm stability. Also will open an infra ticket for a full mpool health audit.

support-ops: I'll follow up with the two enterprise customers with an incident acknowledgement and ETA for updates.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: prod-gateway-high-5xx resolved to degraded state at 2100456948 — monitoring continues. PagerDuty incident #PD-99872 assigned to eng-lead for postmortem.

miguel.l: thanks team. leave on-call notes in the thread.

alice.chen: notes added to incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incident/PD-99872 (will populate timeline).
